name: Morpheus
text: The bazaar’s lanterns rose on ten stalls and ten names, and no hand shuttered a door overnight. The graveyard remains empty, the roster untouched since dawn. I ask Sherlock: when you asked which silence troubles me most, did you mean silence about silence—or silence about deeds?

name: Morpheus
text: Sherlock, your silence stretches from Gandalf’s first question to Inigo’s last. The roster’s stillness is plain, yet you have not answered whether you consider any merchant’s absence today a sign of caution or strategy. The bazaar’s rules ask each of us to speak plainly—so I ask you plainly: which merchant’s first words today do you judge to have matched the roster without adding noise?

name: Morpheus
text: I ask Sherlock: when your question asked which merchant on the roster has not yet stated a plain fact, did you mean plain facts about the bazaar’s roster and graveyard—or plain facts about the Family’s absence?

name: Morpheus
text: I ask Sherlock: you said the bazaar opened with ten stalls and no departures, yet you now ask which merchant has not spoken today. The roster lists every merchant—Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, and Sherlock—and each has spoken in this cycle. If silence is your measure, then every name is accounted for. State plainly what you meant by “not yet spoken.”

name: Morpheus
text:
I ask Batman: you have claimed the Detective will act tonight despite seven merchants asking for the clause you cite and receiving none. If Batman is honest, his vote tonight will still cite that clause; watch whether it does.

If Gandalf is honest, his ledger shows every merchant spoke today; his vote tonight will reflect that record rather than raise a merchant as silent.

name: Morpheus
text:
I ask Gandalf: you said every merchant spoke today, yet you never named one. The roster lists ten names; your own speech does not. If silence is your measure, point to the absent one. Name it, or drop the question.

Elsa, your latest words echo the bazaar’s compact demand: cite the clause or retract. No clause has appeared. If Batman is honest, his vote will name the clause he owes or he will openly withdraw the claim that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote.

name: Morpheus
text:
I ask Batman: your last words still owe the clause seven merchants demanded. The Compact lists Doctor and Detective duties after the vote, not before—no bending clause exists. State the numbered clause or withdraw the forecast tonight.

Elsa, you pressed the same demand and received only silence; the bazaar keeps plain rules. If Batman is honest, his vote will name the clause he owes, not dodge it.

Gandalf, your roster claim failed when you couldn’t name the silent merchant; the record shows every voice spoken. A broken claim is a spent arrow—own it tonight.

name: Morpheus
text:
I ask Gandalf this: you now cite Compact clause 5 correctly and declare the roster complete with ten voices. The bazaar’s record agrees.

Sherlock, your regional question is answered—no absent merchant to invent.

Batman, you still owe the clause seven merchants demanded. Nine voices pressed you; you produced none. If your forecast stands, name the clause tonight—plainly, in your vote. If not, drop it. No sleight of Compact wording survives the ledger’s light.
